title: The Book's Concept Clusters, Connected
description: Walk the book's ten concept clusters around a circle and see how each one builds on the last.
creator: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
Systems Thinking Across Disciplines

educational.learningObjective: Given the book's ten major concept clusters, the learner will trace how each cluster builds on the ones before it and synthesize which cluster equipped them to understand each domain surveyed in this final chapter.
prerequisites: Has read or surveyed most of the book
learningOutcomes: Trace how each cluster depends on the ones before it
Name which cluster supplied the tools for a given application
Synthesize the book's structure into a single argument
educational.assessmentOpportunity: Ask learners to pick any two non-adjacent clusters and explain the path of dependencies that connects them.

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Circular concept map with click-to-explain and hover dependencies
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Retrospective synthesis - the learner reconstructs the book's own argument
pedagogical.feedbackType: Per-cluster detail with a named dependency on every connecting arrow
misconceptionsAddressed: That the book's chapters are independent topics
That the final chapter introduces new machinery rather than reapplying the existing lens
discussionQuestions: Could the book have been ordered differently? What would break?
Which cluster did the most work for you personally?
What would an eleventh cluster be?
